title: India product matching and annotation expansion
protocol: Match labels use independently published sources or exact observed pack evidence. Distinct requires a confirmed pack, brand, flavour or formulation difference. Materially ambiguous relationships stay unresolved. Fields missing from a source remain missing unless an explicit packaging annotation is recorded in that item's evidence.
limits: Convenience sample of India-market grocery catalogue records, independently published product evidence and controlled input variants. Multiple pairs can share a product or source within a split. The dataset supports offline evaluation, with limited coverage and no probability calibration. Controlled rows test robustness to input changes. Rights for Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart feeds are outstanding.
historyOverlap: Parent rows preserve the memberships of the 54-case benchmark. Six older Open Food Facts codes from Everest blends and Kissan sauces remain confined to the parent training split. The extension reuses one already evaluated Krackjack Open Food Facts code and family from the earlier 47-pair validation set, and confines both new comparisons using it to validation. Extension test families and GTINs are disjoint from the previously evaluated benchmarks.
annotationSpotCheck: In the parent benchmark, a second reviewer checked the three observed holdout positives and the separate Britannia Bourbon multipack listing. See extension pair decisions and the separate annotation audit for this milestone's review.
